title: The Book Drop
hook: The head librarian gave me one rule: if a book comes through the return slot after nine, don't check it in.
lines: I close the town library on Friday nights, and the head librarian gave me one rule.
If a book comes through the return slot after nine... don't check it in. Leave it in the bin until morning.
Then last Friday, at nine fourteen, I heard the metal slot creak open.
A small black book. No title. No barcode. Just an old paper checkout card, tucked inside the cover.
The names on the card were night clerks. I knew them from the faded photos in the break room.
Next to each name, a date in red ink... the day each one stopped showing up for work.
The last line was empty. Waiting.
I didn't touch it. I turned off the lights, locked the doors, and walked to my car.
Behind me, the return slot creaked open... and stayed open.
When I got home, there was something in my coat pocket.
The checkout card. My name was on the last line... and the red stamp beside it said: Due tonight.
